meta.title: Wing skeleton, joints and feathers by kind
meta.units: fractions of the semi-span (midline to wingtip at full extension) unless named; angles in degrees; elbow angle = interior angle humerus-forearm (180 straight), manus (wrist) angle = interior angle forearm-carpometacarpus (180 straight)

sources.baliga2019: Baliga VB, Szabo I, Altshuler DL (2019) Range of motion in the avian wing is strongly associated with flight behavior and body mass. Sci. Adv. 5: eaaw6670. Data: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.8856161 (CC BY 4.0): AvianMorphology.xlsx (bones, wing length and area, primary and secondary counts) and the cadaver elbow/wrist range-of-motion recordings
sources.harvey2022: Harvey C, Baliga VB, Wong JCM, Altshuler DL, Inman DJ (2022) Birds can transition between stable and unstable states via wing morphing. Nature 603: 648-653. Data: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5503989 (CC BY 4.0): bones, spans, per-feather lengths and vane widths, 3D wing markers through the elbow/wrist range
sources.harvey2021: Harvey C, Baliga VB, Goates CD, Hunsaker DF, Inman DJ (2021) Gull-inspired joint-driven wing morphing allows adaptive longitudinal flight control. J. R. Soc. Interface 18: 20210132. Data: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5275490 (CC BY 4.0): the gull linkage trajectory (Lar_gla.linkage.ext.loess.csv)
sources.harvey2019: Harvey C, Baliga VB, Lavoie P, Altshuler DL (2019) Wing morphing allows gulls to modulate static pitch stability during gliding. J. R. Soc. Interface 16: 20180641 (text, section 3.1): in vivo gliding elbow 90-154 deg, manus 110-173 deg
sources.matloff2020: Matloff LY, Chang E, Feo TJ, Jeffries L, Stowers AK, Thomson C, Lentink D (2020) How flight feathers stick together to form a continuous morphing wing. Science 367: 293-297. Data: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.11369364 (CC BY 4.0): pigeon feather angles vs wrist angle, per-feather slopes
sources.stowers2017: Stowers AK, Matloff LY, Lentink D (2017) How pigeons couple three-dimensional elbow and wrist motion to morph their wings. J. R. Soc. Interface 14: 20170224 (text via PMC5582118)
sources.baier2013: Baier DB, Gatesy SM, Dial KP (2013) Three-dimensional, high-resolution skeletal kinematics of the avian wing and shoulder during ascending flapping flight and uphill flap-running. PLoS ONE 8: e63982 (CC BY): chukar XROMM, Table 2
sources.featheratlas: The Feather Atlas, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Forensics Laboratory (fws.gov/lab/featheratlas; US federal work): per-feather total and vane lengths (data/featheratlas.sqlite) and scans (outlines digitized here, tools/fa_profiles.py)
sources.alerstam2007: Alerstam T, Rosen M, Baeckman J, Ericson PGP, Hellgren O (2007) Flight speeds among bird species: allometric and phylogenetic effects. PLoS Biol 5: e197 (CC BY), Protocol S1: mass, span, area
sources.wang2011: Wang X, McGowan AJ, Dyke GJ (2011) Avian wing proportions and flight styles. PLoS ONE 6: e28672 (CC BY), Table S1: humerus and ulna (its manus, total-arm and mass columns are inconsistent and are not used)
sources.liu2004: Liu T, Kuykendoll K, Rhew R, Jones S (2004) Avian wings. AIAA 2004-2186 (NASA Langley): a dried gull wing's twist; gull, goose and crane wing extension through the stroke from video

digits.note: no open per-species phalanx data reached: the major digit's phalanges taken as this share of the carpometacarpus

meta.recommended_note: recommended[kind]: bone lengths as fractions of the semi-span (mean of the listed sources, spread = (mean, sd, n)); positions_at_full_extension: the joints' distances out from the midline in the flattened wing at the cadaver's full extension (where markers exist)

planform_at_full_extension.note: cadaver wing at its greatest elbow+manus extension, flattened into its own best-fit plane: [x forward, y out from the midline], fractions of the specimen's measured semi-span; pt8 = tip of P10 (the wingtip only where P10 is the longest primary or nearly: gull, duck); off-plane residuals show how far the cadaver wing departs from flat

linkage.note: the elbow extended by hand, the wrist following through the forearm linkage

in_vivo_gliding.note: glaucous-winged x western gulls gliding; lower elbow angles in stronger wind (-0.61 deg per m/s; gusts -0.40 deg per m/s)

harvey.note: length = vane + calamus; rachis_at_chord_frac = outer (leading) vane width / total width: where the shaft sits along the feather's own chord (0 leading edge)

emargination_digitized.note: steps where a vane narrows, at a fraction of the feather's length from its base; drop = the inward move of the edge over the vane's proximal width. Digitized from the scan outlines (tools/fa_profiles.py; 11.6-45 px/cm; edge +-1 px, position +-0.05 of length); steps past 0.75 of the length are the tip's rounding and are excluded

gull.from_: harvey2022 (L. glaucescens), baliga2019 (L. glaucescens, L. delawarensis), wang2011+alerstam2007 (L. argentatus)

positions_at_full_extension.normalised_to: the larger of the measured semi-span and the P10 tip (1.154)

goose.from_: harvey2022 (B. canadensis), wang2011+alerstam2007 (B. canadensis, A. anser); cmc/digits split by the derived ratio

positions_at_full_extension.normalised_to: the larger of the measured semi-span and the P10 tip (1.112)
positions_at_full_extension.caution: the goose cadaver reached elbow 118 deg only: not a spread wing

swan.estimate: shoulder offset taken from the goose (0.097); manus from the goose's manus/ulna (1.09)

stork.estimate: CMC from the heron's CMC/ulna (0.489); shoulder offset between heron (0.030) and pelican (0.065)

positions_proxy_pelican.normalised_to: the larger of the measured semi-span and the P10 tip (1.072)

heron.from_: harvey2022 (A. herodias; its "cmc" is the CMC alone), wang2011+alerstam2007 (A. cinerea); baliga2019's heron left out (its wing length, 0.63 m, is far short of the species' semi-span)

positions_at_full_extension.normalised_to: the larger of the measured semi-span and the P10 tip (1.000)

ibis.estimate: CMC from the heron's CMC/ulna; shoulder offset estimated

crow.from_: baliga2019 (C. caurinus), wang2011+alerstam2007 (C. corone); shoulder offset from the raven (harvey2022)

positions_at_full_extension_raven.normalised_to: the larger of the measured semi-span and the P10 tip (1.000)
